whoqol-bref.name: WHOQOL-BREF: physical health and health-care items

q2.name: Q2 Satisfaction with health
q2.passage: A2 Is he/she satisfied with his/her health?

q3.name: Q3 Pain stops you doing what you need to do
q3.passage: A3 Does (physical) pain stop him/her from doing what he/she needs to do?

q4.name: Q4 Need for medical treatment to function
q4.passage: A4 Does he/she need any medical treatment to help him/her in his/her daily life?

q10.name: Q10 Energy for everyday life
q10.passage: A10 Do you have enough energy for everyday life?

q11.name: Q11 Accepting your bodily appearance
q11.passage: A11 Are you able to accept your bodily appearance?

q15.name: Q15 Getting around
q15.passage: A15 How well are you able to get around?

q16.name: Q16 Sleep
q16.passage: A16 How satisfied are you with your sleep?

q17.name: Q17 Daily living activities
q17.passage: A17 How satisfied are you with your ability to perform your daily living activities?

q18.name: Q18 Capacity for work
q18.passage: A18 How satisfied are you with your capacity for work?

q24.name: Q24 Access to health services
q24.passage: A24 How satisfied are you with your access to health and social services?

sdg-goal3.name: UN SDG Goal 3 targets (good health and well-being)

3.1.name: 3.1 Reduce maternal mortality
3.1.passage: By 2030, reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births

3.2.name: 3.2 End preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5

3.3.name: 3.3 End epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases

3.4.name: 3.4 Reduce premature mortality from non-communicable diseases
3.4.passage: By 2030, reduce by one third premature mortality from non-communicable diseases

3.5.name: 3.5 Prevention and treatment of substance abuse
3.5.passage: Strengthen the prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drug abuse and harmful use of alcohol

3.6.name: 3.6 Halve deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents
3.6.passage: By 2020, halve the number of global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents

3.7.name: 3.7 Universal access to sexual and reproductive health-care services

3.8.name: 3.8 Universal health coverage
3.8.passage: Achieve universal health coverage, including financial risk protection,

3.9.name: 3.9 Reduce deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals and pollution

3.b.name: 3.b Access to affordable essential medicines and vaccines
3.b.passage: provide access to affordable essential medicines and vaccines,

cdc-health.name: CDC and NCHS: U.S. adult health statistics (chronic pain, disability, chronic disease, obesity, sleep)

chronic-pain.name: Chronic pain
chronic-pain.passage: In 2023, 24.3% of adults had chronic pain

high-impact-pain.name: High-impact chronic pain (frequently limits life or work)
high-impact-pain.passage: 8.5% of adults had chronic pain that frequently limited life or work

any-disability.name: Any disability
any-disability.passage: More than 1 in 4 U.S. adults have some type of disability.

chronic-conditions.name: At least one chronic condition
chronic-conditions.passage: Three in four American adults have at least one chronic condition, and over half have two or more chronic conditions.

obesity.name: Obesity
obesity.passage: The prevalence of obesity among U.S. adults 20 and over was 41.9% during 2017–March 2020.

severe-obesity.name: Severe obesity
severe-obesity.passage: During the same time, the prevalence of severe obesity among U.S. adults was 9.2%.

insufficient-sleep.name: Not getting enough sleep
insufficient-sleep.passage: In 2022, it ranged from 30% of adults in Vermont to 46% adults in Hawaii.

kff-health-care.name: KFF polls: health care costs, insurance problems and treatment by providers

hard-to-afford.name: Difficult to afford health care costs
hard-to-afford.passage: very or somewhat difficult for them to afford their health care costs (44%)

worried-afford.name: Worried about affording health care
worried-afford.passage: about six in ten saying they are "very" (27%) or "somewhat worried" (35%)

skipped-care.name: Skipped or postponed needed care because of cost
skipped-care.passage: Roughly three in ten adults (28%) say that they have skipped or postponed getting needed health care

not-filled-rx.name: Did not fill a prescription because of cost
not-filled-rx.passage: a quarter (27%) who have not filled a prescription

cut-pills.name: Cut pills in half or skipped doses because of cost
cut-pills.passage: one in five (19%) who have cut pills in half or skipped doses of medicine because of the cost

medical-debt.name: Debt from medical or dental bills
medical-debt.passage: In 2022, about four in ten adults (41%) reported having debt due to medical or dental bills

insurance-problems.name: Problems when using health insurance
insurance-problems.passage: roughly 6 in 10 insured adults experience problems when they use their insurance.

denied-claims.name: Denied insurance claims
denied-claims.passage: found that 18% of insured adults say they experienced denied claims in the past year.

negative-provider.name: Negative experiences with a health care provider (ignored, blamed, assumptions made)
negative-provider.passage: A third of adults overall report at least one of several negative experiences with a health care provider

who-fact-sheets.name: WHO fact sheets: common conditions (hearing, vision, oral health, infertility, headache)

hearing-loss.name: Hearing loss
hearing-loss.passage: By 2050, nearly 2.5 billion people are projected to have some degree of hearing loss

vision-impairment.name: Vision impairment
vision-impairment.passage: Globally, at least 2.2 billion people have a near or distance vision impairment.

oral-disease.name: Oral diseases
oral-disease.passage: It is estimated that oral diseases affect nearly 3.7 billion people.

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.passage: Estimates suggest that approximately one in every six people of reproductive age worldwide experience infertility

headache-disorders.name: Headache disorders
headache-disorders.passage: headache disorders affect approximately 40% of the population, or 3.1 billion people in 2021

mhf-body-image-2019.name: Mental Health Foundation (UK) body image survey, 2019

shame.name: Felt shame because of body image
shame.passage: one in five (20 per cent) said they had felt "shame" because of their body image in the last year.

suicidal-thoughts.name: Suicidal thoughts or feelings because of body image
suicidal-thoughts.passage: Just over one in eight UK adults (13 per cent) have experienced suicidal thoughts or feelings
